response.overview: Following the morning roll call, the group—comprising SS members, men from the Reich Labour Service (RAD), and scholars—heads toward an excavation site in Bärhorst, near Nauen, west of Berlin. An animated map reveals other Germanic settlements in the area. A narrator explains the significance of the suffix "—horst." The scene shifts to the excavation site, which takes the form of a long trench. All equipment and tools required for the excavation work are presented. The remains of a house post are discovered, uncovered, and recorded to scale on a drafting sheet. Post holes are excavated. The narrator explains the importance of these findings, which allow for the reconstruction of the original house structures.
response.title: Deutsche Vergangenheit wird lebendig
